description: Cross-binding conformance for how far an `operator_compose` merged-away rename REACHES (esm-libraries-spec §4.7.1 step 4). A renaming match — a `translate` match, or the bare-name fallback #216 resolves by ownership — folds `B.x` into `A.x`, so `B.x` is DELETED and every equation in the document is rewritten off the dead spelling. That rewrite is document-wide over EQUATION ASTs and nothing else, and three other places address the state BY NAME: a `couple` connector's `from`/`to` and a `variable_map`'s `from`/`to`, which are plain scoped-reference STRINGS on the entry object; the override keys a runner is handed; and a surviving expression-template registry body. §4.7.5 step 3 applies every `operator_compose` BEFORE any `couple` or `variable_map`, so an entry that has not run yet can still name a spelling the merge has already deleted. The decision this category pins is RESOLUTION, not refusal: a reference to a merged-away name resolves to the survivor, so a document that merges `B.x` onto `A.x` stays addressable by either spelling. Refusing instead would be defensible for a name nothing can resolve, but these are renames the author ASKED for — a `translate` map names the surviving spelling on purpose — and a document is built around them. Like `operator_compose_merge` and `override_key_diagnostics` this category carries no golden: what it pins is REACH, asserted as structure (which names survive, which equations reference what) rather than as numbers.

flatten._comment: The rewrite is a pure structural transform, so a rewrite-only port implements it in full. All five bindings are in scope.

override_keys._comment: The runner half: a caller's `initial_conditions` / `parameter_overrides` key naming the deleted spelling. Only the three EXECUTING bindings have an override-key surface at all — the same scope split `override_key_diagnostics` records.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no override-key surface
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no override-key surface

output_selection._comment: The OUTPUT half: a name-keyed read of a finished run, and a name-keyed output REQUEST. Only the three EXECUTING bindings have a result object or an output plan at all — the same scope split `override_key_diagnostics` and `output_derivation` record.

scope_excluded.go: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no result object and no output selection
scope_excluded.typescript: rewrite-only port; no simulator, so no result object and no output selection

merged_variable_renames_field._comment: The map flatten records on its metadata so a consumer that addresses a state by name can resolve a spelling the merge moved. Named per binding; the CONTENT is the cross-binding contract.

cases.note: The QUIET failure. A `couple` connector targets `Sink.O3`, which the earlier compose deleted; the connector's `to` is a plain string the equation retarget never reaches, so the target matched nothing and the whole connector was dropped — leaving a flattened tendency arithmetically identical to a document with no `couple` entry at all. `Emis.flux` in `D(Chem.O3, t)` is what the fix is observable as.

The LOUD failure, and the sharper half. A later `variable_map` names the deleted `Sink.O3` as its `from`, so the substitution injected a name the flattened system no longer declares into every equation referencing `Consumer.bg` — a dangling reference that surfaces far downstream as an unbound variable at the build boundary, not a missing term.

A caller's initial-condition key naming the deleted spelling. Unresolved it designates nothing: the key is silently dropped (Python, Julia) or reported unknown (Rust), and the state runs from its declared 30.0 — a wrong answer, not a missing one, because the run still reports a verdict. `parameter_overrides` shares this canonicalization, but a merged-away name is always a DEPENDENT VARIABLE (a state or an observed) and never a parameter, so the state side is where the case actually lands.

A caller reading the finished run by the deleted spelling. The trajectory it names MOVED to `Chem.O3`'s row, so the read resolves there rather than reporting a variable that never existed — and the row NAMES still report only the surviving spelling, because resolving a read must not invent a name the flattened system does not declare. Where a binding also takes an output REQUEST (an `output_observed` / `--observed` list, an `observed_field` lookup), the same map resolves it before the plan is derived.
